subject: Custom SLA & order form language for NovaCare deployment
messages:
From: Chris Miller <chris.miller@novacare.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA / uptime & latency commitments - NovaCare order form

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're excited about Redwood as a replacement for our inference layer. As we move toward procurement, legal has asked for explicit uptime and latency commitments to be captured in an addendum to the MSA (or in the SOW/order form if that's easier). High-level asks from NovaCare: 

- Target uptime: 99.99% monthly for production endpoints (region: us-west)
- P95 inference latency requirement: <= 450ms for standard text-gen requests (98th percentile during business hours is ok to define)
- Incident response: initial acknowledgment for Sev1 within 4 hours; mitigation plan within 24 hours

Can Redwood provide a redlined SLA addendum we can attach to our order form? Also please indicate any exceptions (maintenance windows, force majeure) and whether dedicated capacity is required to meet 99.99%.

Attached: NovaCare_SOW_v3.pdf (for context)

If you can send a proposed addendum and a draft order form line item for Dedicated vs Hosted options, we can route to procurement and legal.

Best,
Chris Miller
Director, Platform Ops
NovaCare Health
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Chris Miller <chris.miller@novacare.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SLA / uptime & latency commitments - NovaCare order form

Hi Chris — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the SOW.

Short answers up-front: yes, we can produce a redlined SLA addendum and order form language. There are two implementation paths that affect commitments and pricing:

1) Hosted (shared capacity): we can commit to a 99.9% uptime SLO with targeted latency p95 SLAs in the order form and SLA addendum; exceptions apply during planned maintenance and capacity saturation events. For 99.99% we'd generally recommend Dedicated capacity.

2) Dedicated: can support 99.99% with an agreed maintenance window and operational runbook; this is the recommended route for mission-critical production workloads that require that uptime target.

I'll loop Legal for the contractual language and SE (Aditya) to validate the latency measurement and whether the 450ms p95 is attainable on your workload profile. Attached an initial template we typically use for enterprise addenda.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to draft redline (SLA addendum + order form) — target delivery by 2026-05-14
- NovaCare to confirm whether you want to price Dedicated vs Hosted for the order form by 2026-05-15
- 30-min sync if helpful — propose Wed 2026-05-13 10:00 PT

Attaching: Redwood_Initial_SLA_Templates.pdf

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-11 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: SLA / uptime & latency commitments - NovaCare order form

Thanks — reviewed SOW and initial template. A few clarifying questions before I prepare a redline: 

- Liability & remedies: does NovaCare expect service credits only, or a broader set of remedies? Our standard is service credits capped at subscription fees for the affected period; customers sometimes request higher caps for mission-critical deployments.
- Measurement window: confirm whether NovaCare wants monthly uptime (calendar month) or rolling 30-day window. Also need to confirm the measurement source (Redwood logs vs external synthetic pings).
- Support & response times: Laura noted 4-hour ack for Sev1 — we typically commit to 1-hour ack for Dedicated enterprise SLAs; for Hosted we do 4-hour ack with escalation. Is 4-hour sufficient, or do they require 1-hour?
- Audit & data residency: do they require audit rights or on-prem evidence (SOC2 reports)? If data residency is required in us-west, note that Dedicated is required for strict residency/policy controls.

I'll draft a redline that includes: definition of SLOs (uptime + p95 latency), measurement method, remedies (service credit table tied to % uptime), exclusions, support definitions (severity matrix, response/mitigation timelines), and a clause for order form language to specify Dedicated/Hosted selection and pricing.

Attaching draft snippet: SLA_Remedies_Draft.docx

-Monica
General Counsel (Contracts) | Redwood Inference
From: Chris Miller <chris.miller@novacare.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@novacare.ai>
Date: 2026-05-11 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SLA / uptime & latency commitments - NovaCare order form

Laura / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Answers to Monica's questions: 

- Remedies: NovaCare is comfortable with service credits as the primary remedy but is going to ask for a cap of up to 6 months' subscription fees for repeated or severe breaches. We understand this is above standard; please flag if that's a blocker.
- Measurement: monthly calendar month is preferred. Measurement will be via Redwood's metrics; we'd like the option to present our own synthetic results as supplementary evidence in disputes.
- Support: 4-hour ack is OK; we expect a 4-hour ack and a 24-hour mitigation plan for Sev1. If Redwood can offer 1-hour for Dedicated at a premium, please include that in the order form options.
- Audit: we will request SOC2 and a brief evidence package (logs retention, incident history) during procurement. Data residency in us-west is required for production; Dedicated preferred.

We want the redline back no later than 2026-05-20 so we can sign and get procurement approvals on the same cycle. Also please include a DocuSign-ready order form.

Thanks,
Chris
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Chris Miller <chris.miller@novacare.ai>

Subject: RE: SLA / uptime & latency commitments - NovaCare order form

Chris — appreciate the clarity and the timeline. Plan recap and next steps: 

1) Redwood will deliver a redline of the SLA addendum and a DocuSign-ready order form with two priced options (Hosted: 99.9% + 4-hour ack; Dedicated: 99.99% + 1-hour ack) by 2026-05-14.
2) Legal will include a service credit table tying monthly uptime % to credit % and will call out the proposed 6-month cap request as a negotiation point (we'll flag in the redline).
3) SE (Aditya) will annotate the addendum with latency measurement methodology and an appendix describing typical workload headroom; he will also validate whether the 450ms p95 target is achievable without Dedicated.
4) We'll attach SOC2 report and retention/config documentation to the procurement packet.

Attached: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v0.2.docx, Redwood_OrderForm_NovaCare_Quote.pdf
